## C2 — KG handoff hints: Vision and Health

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-R01 | anchor: A01
Driver fitness duty means the motorist stays healthy enough to drive and reports risky conditions to the Division after HCP review [A01]
Why it matters: prereq_hint none; group_hint fitness-responsibility; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with review-triggers.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-R02 | anchor: A80
For a regular Class D vehicle, vision must reach twenty over forty in at least one eye, with a field of vision measuring at least ninety degrees. A vision test is required when visiting a field office, or when applying for a license at an age older than sixty-five [A80].
Why it matters: prereq_hint R01; group_hint vision-and-categories; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with CVE-versus-FAE forms.
Source: [A80 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-R03 | anchor: A02
Mind-state and medication caution says anger, confusion, distraction, citations and sedating doses warn against driving until calm and dosed safely [A02]
Why it matters: prereq_hint R01; group_hint mental-alertness; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with alcohol-drugs versus illness.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-R04 | anchor: A81
After a completed driver review, the hearing officer considers the medical evaluation and the person's driving needs, roads and traffic, then decides on restrictions using Medical Advisory Board guidelines. When the review is completed, privileges are withdrawn only if the division finds safe driving impossible under any conditions. Failing to complete a required review also causes withdrawal [A81].
Why it matters: prereq_hint R01; group_hint review-process; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with voluntary-report versus ordered-review.
Source: [A81 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0032]
